---
title: "Figure 4—figure supplement 11 — what the distortion is made of: affine distance of the sample and correlation distortion, resolved over the design space"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
THE DECOMPOSITION of supplement 10's whole-matrix distortion into its two causes, each as an
affine-invariant distance to the identity, mapped over the same plane, two blocks (sample,
correlation) x algorithm.

The Gaussian information distortion factors into two congruences: the SAMPLE distortion (G^{-1/2}
J_sample G^{-1/2}, the per-sample departure from the Gaussian the algorithm assumes — skewness and
kurtosis of the one-step residual) and the CORRELATION distortion (J_sample^{-1/2} J J_sample^{-1/2},
the temporal memory across steps that a diagonal-in-time likelihood ignores). Neither is emitted as
an affine distance, but both are emitted as DENSE matrices, so the distance is computed here as
d_AI(M, I) = sqrt(sum_i (log lambda_i)^2) over their eigenvalues.

WHY BOTH, AND WHY IT MATTERS. The two naive algorithms fail for DIFFERENT reasons, and the split
shows it. Measured (N_ch 1e4, noise 1): NR's distortion is mostly CORRELATION (29 vs sample 20) — it
models a per-time variance but throws away the off-diagonal, so the memory it discards is its dominant
error. LSE's is mostly SAMPLE (2.1 vs correlation 0.78) — marginalising the noise scale, its residual
is dominated by per-sample non-Gaussianity rather than by retained temporal structure. R and IR carry
almost neither (all < 0.05 for IR). So the recursion cures the CORRELATION part, and only conditioning
the interval (IR over R) cleans up the residual sample part at coarse Delta.

CAVEAT: the correlation distortion is a truncated-kernel estimate (max_lag = 10). Its affine distance
is an integrated-memory scalar in the same family as supplement 9's score integral-lag, but on the
distortion matrix rather than the score. Scale shared with supplement 10.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
source("figure_4_common.R")
```

```{r scale}
AFF_LIN    <- c(0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30)
AFF_BREAKS <- log10(AFF_LIN)
AFF_PAL    <- colorRampPalette(RAMP[7:13], space = "Lab")(length(AFF_LIN) - 1)
AFF_LAB    <- fmt_big(AFF_LIN)
AFF_SOL    <- 0.5
AFF_DSH    <- 2
```

```{r data}
# affine distance of one dense distortion matrix to the identity, per (algo, cell, interval)
NP <- c(nonlinearsqr = 4, macro_NR = 6, macro_R = 6, macro_IR = 6)
COMP <- c(sample = "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Sample_Distortion",
          correlation = "Probit_statistics_Likelihood_Correlation_Distortion")

aff_mat <- function(sub, p) {              # sub: rows for ONE (component, interval) at probit==mean
  M <- matrix(NA, p, p)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(sub))) M[sub$value_row[i] + 1, sub$value_col[i] + 1] <- sub$v[i]
  M <- (M + t(M)) / 2
  e <- eigen(M, symmetric = TRUE)$values
  if (any(!is.finite(e)) || any(e <= 0)) return(NA_real_)
  sqrt(sum(log(e)^2))
}

lag_aff <- imap_dfr(GRID_BY_ALGO, function(g, a) if (!nrow(g)) tibble() else {
  p <- NP[[a]]
  pmap_dfr(g, function(nch, z) {
    raw <- read.csv(findf(nch, a, z, "battery_pool_G"), skip = 1) %>%
      filter(component_path %in% COMP, statistic == "value", probit == "mean")
    imap_dfr(COMP, function(cp, nm) raw %>% filter(component_path == cp) %>%
      group_by(interval_in_tau, value_row, value_col) %>% summarise(v = mean(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
      group_by(interval_in_tau) %>% group_modify(~ tibble(m = aff_mat(.x, p))) %>%
      mutate(algo = a, noise = z, Num_ch = nch, part = nm))
  })
}) %>%
  filter(is.finite(m)) %>%
  mutate(param = part,                    # two synthetic "parameters": the two distortion parts
         lx = log10(interval_in_tau), ly = log10(as.numeric(noise)),
         nchf = factor(paste0("N[ch]==", Num_ch), levels = paste0("N[ch]==", NCHS)))

PARAM_MATH["sample"] <- "sample"
PARAM_MATH["correlation"] <- "correlation"
cat("affine distance by part and algorithm (median over grid):\n")
print(as.data.frame(lag_aff %>% group_by(part, algo) %>% summarise(m = median(m), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = algo, values_from = m)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
sat(log10(lag_aff$m), min(AFF_BREAKS), max(AFF_BREAKS), "affine distance")
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 9.5}
hC <- map_height(length(COMP), 0.475)
g <- btitle("Distortion decomposed: affine distance of the sample and correlation parts") /
     mapblock(lag_aff, function(d) log10(d$m), AFF_PAL, AFF_BREAKS, names(COMP),
              top = TRUE, bottom = TRUE, iso_sol = log10(AFF_SOL), iso_dsh = log10(AFF_DSH)) /
     colorbar(AFF_PAL, AFF_LAB, "affine distance", AFF_LIN, sol = AFF_SOL, dsh = AFF_DSH)
hs <- c(0.16, hC, 0.28)
g <- g + plot_layout(heights = hs)
g
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_11.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = sum(hs))
```

```{r render-byNch, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 11}
# TRANSPOSED sibling (Luciano, 2026-07-25): columns = algorithm, rows = N_ch, proportional row height.
.pw <- names(COMP)
.gg <- lapply(.pw, function(p) mapblock_byNch(lag_aff, function(d) log10(d$m), AFF_PAL, AFF_BREAKS,
              p, top = TRUE, bottom = TRUE, iso_sol = log10(AFF_SOL), iso_dsh = log10(AFF_DSH)))
g <- Reduce(`/`, c(list(btitle("Distortion decomposed, sample & correlation affine parts (transposed: algo x N_ch)")),
                   .gg, list(colorbar(AFF_PAL, AFF_LAB, "affine distance", AFF_LIN, sol = AFF_SOL, dsh = AFF_DSH))))
hs <- c(0.16, rep(map_height_byNch(1, 0.45), length(.pw)), 0.28)
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_11_byNch.pdf", g + plot_layout(heights = hs), width = 7.0, height = sum(hs))
```
